lessons.title: Getting Started: What a Computer Is and What It Does
lessons.notes_html:
What is a computer?

A computer is a machine that works on given instructions. It works fast and accurately, stores a large amount of data, and repeats the same work again and again without getting tired. It can do many kinds of work in different fields.

How a computer works — the block diagram

PartWork
Input devicesData comes in (left side of the diagram)
Memory (inside the CPU)Holds the data
Control Unit (inside the CPU)Directs all the parts
ALU (inside the CPU)Does the calculations — addition, subtraction, multiplication, division and comparison
Output devicesThe result goes out (right side of the diagram)

Uses of the computer in daily life

  • Education: teaching and learning, school management and online learning.
  • Health: doctors keep patients' records and use computers for tests and guidance in treatment.
  • Other fields: banking, business, agriculture and communication — the computer makes everyday work easier in all of them.

mcqs.q: Which part of the CPU does calculations such as addition, subtraction, multiplication, division and comparison?
mcqs.why: The ALU (Arithmetic Logic Unit) solves arithmetic and logical calculations — addition, subtraction, multiplication, division and comparison — inside the CPU.

mcqs.q: Which statement correctly matches an input device?
options: Large storage capacity and permanent state
Hardware and a tool that enters data into the computer
mcqs.why: An input device is hardware — a tool that enters data into the computer, such as the keyboard, mouse and scanner.

mcqs.q: In the block diagram of a computer, which parts are found inside the CPU?
options: Hard disk, USB and SD card
mcqs.why: Inside the CPU there are three parts: memory (holding data), the control unit (directing all parts) and the ALU (doing calculations). Input and output devices stay outside.

mcqs.q: In the block diagram, data enters the computer from which side and the result leaves from which side?
options: Data and result both pass through the memory only
The result comes in and data goes out
Both data and result pass through the printer
Data comes in from the input side and the result goes out from the output side
mcqs.why: On the left side of the block diagram are the input devices, from where data comes in; on the right side are the output devices, from where the result goes out.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is an important feature of a computer?
options: It works fast and accurately and never gets tired of repeating work
It works slowly but never makes a mistake in storing data
It can work without any instructions
It stores only a small amount of data
mcqs.why: The computer works fast and accurately on given instructions, stores a large amount of data, and repeats the same work without getting tired.

mcqs.q: How is the computer used in the field of education?
options: For teaching and learning, school management and online learning
mcqs.why: In education, the computer is used for teaching and learning, school management and online learning, as given in the book.

mcqs.q: How do doctors use computers in the health field?
options: For school management and online learning
For patients' records, tests and guidance in treatment
mcqs.why: In health, doctors use computers for patients' records, tests and guidance in treatment.

mcqs.q: What is the work of the Control Unit inside the CPU?
options: Showing the result on the screen
Directing all the parts of the computer
mcqs.why: The control unit directs all parts of the computer; doing calculations is the ALU's work and holding data is the memory's work.

mcqs.q: Which of these fields is helped by computers, according to the book?
mcqs.why: Besides education and health, the computer makes everyday work easier in banking, business, agriculture and communication.

mcqs.q: A computer can repeat the same work again and again because…
options: it has a very small memory
it does not get tired like a human being
mcqs.why: One of the important features of a computer is that it repeats the same work without getting tired, and keeps working fast and accurately.

lessons.title: Evolution of Computers and the Five Generations
lessons.notes_html:
The eras of computer evolution

  • Mechanical era: the era of hand-operated machines, such as the abacus.
  • Electro-mechanical era: machines such as Hollerith's tabulating machine.
  • Electronic era: the five generations of electronic computers.

The five generations of computers

GenerationPeriodTechnologyExamples
First1940–1956Vacuum tubeENIAC, UNIVAC
Second1956–1965TransistorIBM 7094, IBM 1401
Third1964–1971Integrated circuit (IC)IBM 360, IBM 370
Fourth1971 to todayMicroprocessorIBM PC, Macintosh
FifthToday onwardsArtificial intelligence (AI)Robots, expert systems

Timeline of major changes

Mechanical era: abacus, Napier's bones, slide rule, Pascaline and Leibniz's calculator → electro-mechanical era: Hollerith's tabulating machine → electronic era: vacuum tube, transistor, integrated circuit, microprocessor and artificial intelligence.

The Graphical User Interface (GUI) first appeared in the fourth generation, along with the microprocessor.

mcqs.q: In which generation did the Graphical User Interface (GUI) first appear?
mcqs.why: In the fourth generation, the Graphical User Interface was introduced along with the microprocessor.

mcqs.q: Which technology was used in the first generation of computers?
mcqs.why: The first generation (1940–1956) used vacuum tubes; ENIAC and UNIVAC are its examples.

mcqs.q: ENIAC and UNIVAC are examples of which generation?
mcqs.why: ENIAC and UNIVAC are examples of the first generation of computers, which used vacuum tubes during 1940–1956.

mcqs.q: Which technology belongs to the second generation (1956–1965)?
mcqs.why: The second generation used transistors; IBM 7094 and IBM 1401 are its examples.

mcqs.q: IBM 360 and IBM 370 are examples of which generation?
mcqs.why: IBM 360 and IBM 370 are third-generation computers (1964–1971), which used integrated circuits (IC).

mcqs.q: The fourth generation of computers is based on which technology?
mcqs.why: The fourth generation (1971 to today) is based on the microprocessor; the IBM PC and Macintosh are its examples.

mcqs.q: Robots and expert systems are examples of which generation?
mcqs.why: The fifth generation (today onwards) is based on artificial intelligence (AI); robots and expert systems are its examples.

mcqs.q: Which statement correctly matches the mechanical era?
mcqs.why: The mechanical era was the era of hand-operated machines — early machines were run by hand, such as the abacus.

mcqs.q: Which machines belong to the mechanical era in the timeline of computer evolution?
options: Abacus, Napier's bones, slide rule, Pascaline and Leibniz's calculator
mcqs.why: The mechanical era includes the abacus, Napier's bones, the slide rule, the Pascaline and Leibniz's calculator.

mcqs.q: Hollerith's tabulating machine belongs to which era?
mcqs.why: In the timeline of computer evolution, Hollerith's tabulating machine belongs to the electro-mechanical era, between the mechanical and electronic eras.

lessons.title: Types of Computers
lessons.notes_html:
Analogue, digital and hybrid computers

TypeHow it worksExamples around us
AnalogueWorks on continuous measurementSpeedometer, voltmeter
DigitalProcessing using the binary system (0 and 1)Desktop computer, laptop, mobile phone
HybridConverts analogue measurement into digital numbersHospital measuring instruments, petrol pump machines

Computers by size and power

  • Super computer: the most powerful and the most expensive of all; used for large scientific calculations.
  • Mainframe computer
  • Mini computer
  • Micro computer: called a personal computer (PC) — for the personal use of one person.

mcqs.q: Which computers are the most expensive of all?
mcqs.why: Super computers are the most powerful and most expensive, and are used for large scientific calculations.

mcqs.q: Which statement correctly matches a digital computer?
options: Large storage capacity and permanent state
mcqs.why: A digital computer works on 0 and 1 (binary) — it does its processing using the binary system.

mcqs.q: Which statement correctly matches a micro computer?
options: The most powerful and expensive computer
A machine that only measures continuous values
PC — a personal computer for the personal use of one person
Hardware that enters data into the computer
mcqs.why: A micro computer is called a personal computer (PC), which is for the personal use of one person.

mcqs.q: A speedometer and a voltmeter are examples of which type of computer?
mcqs.why: Analogue computers work on continuous measurement; the speedometer and voltmeter around us are their examples.

mcqs.q: A desktop computer, laptop and mobile phone are examples of which type?
mcqs.why: The desktop computer, laptop and mobile phone are digital computers because they process using the binary system.

mcqs.q: Hospital measuring instruments and petrol pump machines are examples of which type of computer?
mcqs.why: Hybrid computers convert analogue measurement into digital numbers; hospital measuring instruments and petrol pump machines are their examples.

mcqs.q: Super computers are mostly used for…
mcqs.why: Super computers are the most powerful and most expensive computers, and are used for large scientific calculations.

mcqs.q: What does a hybrid computer do with analogue measurement?
options: It stores it in a USB disk
It converts it into digital numbers
mcqs.why: A hybrid computer converts analogue measurement into digital numbers, as in hospital measuring instruments and petrol pump machines.

mcqs.q: Which type of computer works on the values 0 and 1?
mcqs.why: A digital computer works on 0 and 1 — the binary system — as stated in the book.

mcqs.q: Which is the smallest computer in the list of computers by size and power?
mcqs.why: In the book's list — super, mainframe, mini and micro — the micro computer (PC) is the smallest, made for one person's personal use.

lessons.title: Hardware: Input, Output and Storage Devices
lessons.notes_html:
Input devices

DeviceFunction
KeyboardEntering writing
MousePointing
ScannerEntering images — converts a paper (hard) copy into a soft copy inside the computer
MicrophoneEntering sound

Output devices

DeviceFunction
MonitorShowing the result
PrinterPrinting on paper
SpeakerProducing sound
ProjectorShowing on a big screen

Printers

  • Impact printer: prints by striking a ribbon onto the paper, e.g. dot-matrix printer.
  • Non-impact printer: prints without striking, e.g. inkjet or laser printer — they give clean and quiet printing.

Storage devices

  • Hard disk: the large-capacity permanent storage fitted inside the computer.
  • USB flash disk: a small, portable storage used to move data from one computer to another.
  • SD card: a tiny memory card mostly used in mobiles, cameras and other small devices.

A secondary storage device has large storage capacity and keeps data in a permanent state, such as a hard disk. For a school, a flat-panel monitor is better than a CRT monitor because it takes less space, uses less electricity and shows a clear picture, while a CRT monitor is heavy and bulky.

mcqs.q: Which device converts a paper (hard) copy into a soft copy inside the computer?
mcqs.why: A scanner converts a printed image or writing on paper into electronic form and feeds it into the computer.

mcqs.q: Which statement correctly matches a secondary storage device?
options: Hardware and a tool that enters data into the computer
Large storage capacity and permanent state
mcqs.why: Secondary storage keeps data saved permanently and has large storage capacity, such as a hard disk.

mcqs.q: What is the function of a scanner as an input device?
mcqs.why: In the book's list of input devices, the scanner is used for entering images; the keyboard enters writing, the mouse points and the microphone enters sound.

mcqs.q: Which output device shows the result on a big screen?
mcqs.why: A projector shows the result on a big screen; a monitor shows it on its own screen and a printer prints it on paper.

mcqs.q: A dot-matrix printer is an example of which kind of printer?
mcqs.why: An impact printer prints by striking a ribbon onto the paper, like a dot-matrix printer.

mcqs.q: Inkjet and laser printers are examples of which kind of printer?
mcqs.why: A non-impact printer prints without striking, like an inkjet or laser printer, which give clean and quiet printing.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between an impact and a non-impact printer?
options: An impact printer strikes a ribbon on the paper; a non-impact printer prints without striking
An impact printer uses light; a non-impact printer uses a ribbon
An impact printer is silent; a non-impact printer is noisy
There is no difference between them
mcqs.why: An impact printer prints by striking a ribbon onto the paper (dot-matrix); a non-impact printer prints without striking (inkjet, laser) and gives clean, quiet printing.

mcqs.q: Which storage device is the large-capacity permanent storage fitted inside the computer?
mcqs.why: A hard disk is the large-capacity permanent storage fitted inside the computer; a USB flash disk is portable and an SD card is a tiny card for small devices.

mcqs.q: A USB flash disk is mainly used for…
options: storing all the data inside the computer permanently
showing pictures on a big screen
moving data from one computer to another
mcqs.why: A USB flash disk is a small, portable storage used to move data from one computer to another.

mcqs.q: An SD card is mostly used in…
options: mobiles, cameras and other small devices
mcqs.why: An SD card is a tiny memory card mostly used in mobiles, cameras and other small devices.

mcqs.q: Which monitor is better for a school — CRT or flat-panel — and why?
options: Flat-panel, because it takes less space, uses less electricity and shows a clear picture
CRT, because it is heavy and bulky
CRT, because it uses more electricity
Flat-panel, because it is heavier than CRT
mcqs.why: For a school a flat-panel monitor is better, because it takes less space, uses less electricity and shows a clear picture, while a CRT monitor is heavy and bulky.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is an output device?
mcqs.why: The speaker is an output device — it produces sound. Keyboard, mouse and microphone are input devices.

mcqs.q: What is the function of a microphone in the computer?
mcqs.why: The microphone is an input device used for entering sound; producing sound is the work of the speaker, an output device.

mcqs.q: Which device is used for pointing in a computer?
mcqs.why: In the book's list, the mouse is the input device used for pointing; the keyboard enters writing and the scanner enters images.

mcqs.q: Why do inkjet and laser printers give better printing than a dot-matrix printer?
options: They print without striking, so the printing is clean and quiet
They strike the ribbon harder on the paper
They use no ink at all
They print only in black colour
mcqs.why: Non-impact printers like inkjet and laser print without striking a ribbon, which gives clean and quiet printing.

lessons.title: Memory and the Motherboard
lessons.notes_html:
Memory

  • RAM is temporary memory — when the power is switched off, the data held in it is lost.
  • The memory that is permanent does not lose its data when the power goes off.

Buses

The data bus is the set of wires that joins the CPU to the main memory — it carries data between the processor and the memory. The book's exercise also names the control bus and the address bus.

The motherboard

Parts found on the motherboard include:

  • Microprocessor (CPU)
  • RAM and ROM
  • Ports and slots
  • Buses
  • BIOS chip
  • Connectors, transistors and diodes

mcqs.q: Which memory is lost when the power goes off?
options: RAM — it is temporary memory and is lost as soon as the power goes off
Hard disk — it stores data permanently
SD card — it is used in mobiles
mcqs.why: RAM is temporary memory; when the power is switched off, the data held in it is lost.

mcqs.q: What is the set of wires that joins the CPU to the main memory called?
mcqs.why: The data bus carries data between the processor and the memory — it is the set of wires joining the CPU to the main memory.

mcqs.q: What does the data bus carry between the processor and the memory?
mcqs.why: The data bus carries data between the processor and the memory.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is a part found on the motherboard?
mcqs.why: The BIOS chip is on the motherboard, along with the microprocessor (CPU), RAM, ROM, ports, slots, buses, connectors, transistors and diodes. The monitor, keyboard and printer are separate devices.

mcqs.q: Which pair of memory parts is found on the motherboard?
mcqs.why: On the motherboard there are the microprocessor (CPU), RAM, ROM, ports, slots, buses, BIOS chip, connectors, transistors and diodes.

mcqs.q: RAM is called temporary memory because…
options: it can never store any data
it is fitted outside the computer
its data is lost when the power is switched off
it is only used in mobiles
mcqs.why: RAM is temporary memory; when the power is switched off, the data held in it is lost — that is why it is called temporary.

mcqs.q: Which of these is NOT listed in the book as a part of the motherboard?
mcqs.why: The book lists the microprocessor (CPU), RAM, ROM, ports, slots, buses, BIOS chip, connectors, transistors and diodes on the motherboard. The speaker is an output device, not a motherboard part.

mcqs.q: The microprocessor fitted on the motherboard is also called the…
mcqs.why: The microprocessor on the motherboard is the CPU — the central processing unit of the computer.

mcqs.q: Which part on the motherboard stores the basic start-up program of the computer?
mcqs.why: The BIOS chip is one of the parts found on the motherboard; the book lists it among the motherboard's parts.

mcqs.q: Ports and slots on the motherboard are used for…
options: joining other parts and devices with the motherboard
mcqs.why: Ports and slots are among the parts found on the motherboard; calculations are done by the CPU/ALU and showing the result is the work of output devices.

lessons.title: Software: System Software, Application Software and Translators
lessons.notes_html:
Hardware and software

Hardware is the visible, touchable physical parts of the computer, such as the motherboard, keyboard and monitor. Software is the set of instructions that makes the computer work, such as the operating system and application programs. Without hardware, software cannot run, and without software, hardware is useless.

System software and application software

System softwareApplication software
Runs the computer's hardware and all its activityDoes some particular job of the user
Examples: operating system, driversExamples: writing a document, doing calculations, playing a game

Without system software, application software cannot run. The operating system is the program that supervises all the work of the computer — a computer cannot run without it. A software engineer is the person expert in writing and running programs.

Kinds of application software (with examples)

KindExamples
BusinessBanking software, accounting software, inventory management
EducationE-learning programs, school management software, learning programs
EntertainmentMedia player, computer game, video program
ProductivityWord processor (documents), spreadsheet, presentation program

Productivity software helps with documents, spreadsheets and presentations. A media player is entertainment software.

Language translators

  • Compiler: translates a whole program written in a high-level language into machine language in one go.
  • Assembler: translates the instructions of a program written in assembly language into machine language.
  • Interpreter is also named in the book as a translation tool.

mcqs.q: What kind of software is a media player?
mcqs.why: Media players and games are software used for entertainment, so a media player is entertainment software.

mcqs.q: Which program supervises all the work of the computer?
mcqs.why: The operating system manages and controls all parts of the computer — it supervises all the work of the computer.

mcqs.q: Which tool do modern (high-level) languages use for translation?
mcqs.why: A compiler translates a whole program written in a high-level language into machine language.

mcqs.q: Without what can a computer not run?
mcqs.why: Without an operating system the computer cannot run its hardware and other programs.

mcqs.q: Who is the person expert in writing and running programs?
mcqs.why: A software engineer writes and runs programs in different programming languages.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between a compiler and an assembler?
options: A compiler translates a whole high-level language program in one go; an assembler translates assembly language instructions
A compiler translates assembly language; an assembler translates high-level language
Both translate only one line at a time
There is no difference between them
mcqs.why: A compiler translates a whole program written in a high-level language into machine language in one go; an assembler translates the instructions of a program written in assembly language into machine language.

mcqs.q: What is hardware?
options: The set of instructions that makes the computer work
The visible, touchable physical parts of the computer, such as the motherboard, keyboard and monitor
Only the programs stored in memory
The data entered by the user
mcqs.why: Hardware is the visible, touchable physical parts of the computer, such as the motherboard, keyboard and monitor; software is the set of instructions.

mcqs.q: Without software, hardware is…
options: useless — and without hardware, software cannot run
mcqs.why: Without hardware, software cannot run, and without software, hardware is useless — the two need each other.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between system software and application software?
options: System software plays games; application software runs the hardware
System software is only for business; application software is only for education
There is no difference between them
System software runs the hardware and all activity; application software does a particular job of the user
mcqs.why: System software runs the computer's hardware and all its activity, such as the operating system and drivers; application software does some particular job of the user. Without system software, application software cannot run.

mcqs.q: Which statement correctly matches productivity software?
options: Large storage capacity and permanent state
mcqs.why: Productivity software helps with documents, spreadsheets and presentations — including spreadsheets and databases.

mcqs.q: Banking software, accounting software and inventory management are examples of which kind of software?
mcqs.why: The book gives banking software, accounting software and inventory management as examples of business software.

mcqs.q: E-learning programs and school management software are examples of which kind of software?
mcqs.why: E-learning programs, school management software and learning programs are the book's examples of education software.

mcqs.q: A word processor, a spreadsheet and a presentation program are examples of which kind of software?
mcqs.why: The book lists the word processor (documents), spreadsheet and presentation program as productivity software.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is system software?
mcqs.why: The operating system is system software — it runs the computer's hardware and all its activity. The others are application software.

mcqs.q: A compiler translates a program written in which language?
mcqs.why: A compiler translates a whole program written in a high-level language into machine language in one go; assembly language is translated by an assembler.

lessons.title: The Operating System and Its Functions
lessons.notes_html:
What is an operating system?

The operating system is the program that runs the computer and manages its files, memory, input/output and external devices. It carries out the basic operations of the computer. Examples: Windows, DOS, Linux, Android, Mac and iOS.

Functions of the operating system

  • Booting — preparing the system
  • Resource management — distribution of resources
  • User interface — contact with the user
  • Memory management
  • Input/output management
  • File management
  • Device management
  • User management

Resource management

In resource management, the operating system manages the distribution (allocation), return (de-allocation) and shared use (shared memory) of hardware and software resources such as the processor, memory, input/output devices and files. The transfer of data between the processor and memory and the control of resources is resource management.

mcqs.q: Which software carries out the basic operations of the computer?
mcqs.why: The operating system runs all the basic operations of the computer.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is an example of an operating system?
mcqs.why: Windows, DOS, Linux, Android, Mac and iOS are the book's examples of operating systems.

mcqs.q: The operating system manages which of the following?
options: Files, memory, input/output and external devices
Only the colours of the screen
Only the documents written by the user
mcqs.why: The operating system is the program that runs the computer and manages its files, memory, input/output and external devices.

mcqs.q: Which statement correctly matches input/output management?
options: It is a type of application software
It is a function of the operating system
It is a kind of malware
It is an office automation program
mcqs.why: Input/output management is one of the functions of the operating system, along with booting, resource management, memory management, file management, device management and user management.

mcqs.q: What is the transfer of data between the processor and memory and the control of resources called?
mcqs.why: In resource management, the operating system distributes and controls the hardware and software resources, including the transfer of data between the processor and memory.

mcqs.q: In resource management, what does the operating system do with resources?
options: Allocation, de-allocation and shared use of resources
mcqs.why: In resource management, the operating system manages the distribution (allocation), return (de-allocation) and shared use (shared memory) of resources such as the processor, memory, input/output devices and files.

mcqs.q: Which resources does the operating system manage in resource management?
options: Processor, memory, input/output devices and files
mcqs.why: The operating system manages hardware and software resources such as the processor, memory, input/output devices and files.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is a function of the operating system?
mcqs.why: File management is a function of the operating system; writing documents, making presentations and playing videos are done by application programs.

mcqs.q: Booting is counted among the functions of the operating system because…
options: it connects the computer to the internet
it prepares the system for work
mcqs.why: Booting — preparing the system — is the first function of the operating system listed in the book.

mcqs.q: DOS and Linux are examples of what?
mcqs.why: DOS and Linux are operating systems, like Windows, Android, Mac and iOS.

lessons.title: Booting, the User Interface and Processes
lessons.notes_html:
Booting

Booting is the process of checking the computer and preparing the operating system for work.

The user interface

The interface is the program that makes contact between the user and the computer possible.

GUI (Graphical User Interface)CLI (Command Line Interface)
Pictures, icons and menus; work is done with mouse clicksCommands have to be typed and remembered
Easy for the ordinary userFast but harder to learn
Examples: Windows, iOSExamples: MS-DOS, Unix

Windows is a well-known operating system with a GUI. A process is the work that the system is doing at that time.

mcqs.q: Which program makes contact with the computer system possible?
mcqs.why: The interface is the program that makes contact between the user and the computer possible.

mcqs.q: What is the process of checking the computer and preparing the operating system for work called?
mcqs.why: In booting, the computer checks its parts and prepares the operating system for work.

mcqs.q: Which statement correctly matches CLI?
options: It is an office automation program
It is the work the system is doing
It is a written-commands interface in which the user types commands
It is a well-known operating system
mcqs.why: CLI is a written-commands interface, in which the user types commands to give instructions to the computer.

mcqs.q: Which statement correctly matches Windows?
options: It is an office automation program
mcqs.why: Windows is a well-known operating system — as the book's matching exercise confirms.

mcqs.q: Which statement correctly matches a process?
options: The work the system is doing
mcqs.why: A process is the work that the system is doing at that time.

mcqs.q: What is the main difference between GUI and CLI?
options: A GUI is only for games; a CLI is only for offices
In a GUI there are pictures, icons and menus used with mouse clicks; in a CLI commands are typed and remembered
A GUI needs no operating system; a CLI does
There is no difference between them
mcqs.why: In a GUI there are pictures, icons and menus, and work is done with mouse clicks, such as Windows and iOS; in a CLI, commands have to be typed and remembered, such as MS-DOS and Unix.

mcqs.q: Which interface is easy for the ordinary user?
mcqs.why: A GUI is easy for the ordinary user; a CLI is fast but harder to learn because its commands must be typed and remembered.

mcqs.q: MS-DOS and Unix are examples of which kind of interface?
mcqs.why: MS-DOS and Unix use a CLI, in which commands have to be typed and remembered.

mcqs.q: Windows and iOS are examples of which kind of interface?
mcqs.why: Windows and iOS have a GUI — pictures, icons and menus, with work done by mouse clicks.

mcqs.q: During booting, the computer…
options: checks its parts and prepares the operating system for work
mcqs.why: Booting is the process of checking the computer and preparing the operating system for work.

lessons.title: Types of Operating Systems
lessons.notes_html:
Single-user and multi-user systems

Single-user OSMulti-user OS
Only one user can work at a timeMany users can work at the same time
Examples: DOS, Windows 98Examples: Unix, Linux

For an institution, a multi-user system is better, because many people can work at the same time and resources are shared. DOS is a single-user operating system — only one user can work at a time.

Batch processing

In batch processing, similar jobs are gathered and run in one batch — the system divides similar jobs into groups.

Real-time systems

Hard real timeSoft real time
Work must be finished within the fixed time; there is no room for delayWork should be finished within the time, but a small delay can be tolerated
Example: traffic control systemExamples: online transactions, multimedia

A real-time operating system finishes work within the fixed time. The book's matching table also pairs the real-time operating system with the time-sharing operating system as types of operating systems.

mcqs.q: With how many users can a multi-user operating system work at the same time?
mcqs.why: In a multi-user system, many users can use the computer at the same time.

mcqs.q: Which operating system divides similar jobs into groups?
mcqs.why: In batch processing, similar jobs are gathered and run in one batch.

mcqs.q: Which system makes sure that work is finished within the fixed time without delay?
mcqs.why: In a hard real-time system, the work must be finished within the fixed time; there is no room for delay.

mcqs.q: DOS is an example of what?
mcqs.why: In DOS, only one user can work at a time, so DOS is a single-user OS.

mcqs.q: Which operating system finishes work within the fixed time?
mcqs.why: In a real-time system, work must be finished within the fixed time limit.

mcqs.q: Unix and Linux are examples of which type of operating system?
mcqs.why: In a multi-user system many users can work at the same time; Unix and Linux are its examples, while DOS and Windows 98 are single-user.

mcqs.q: Which operating system is better for an institution, and why?
options: Multi-user, because many people can work at the same time and resources are shared
Single-user, because only one person can work
Batch processing, because jobs wait in a line
DOS, because it is the oldest system
mcqs.why: For an institution, multi-user is better, because many people can work at the same time and resources are shared.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between soft real time and hard real time?
options: Soft real time is used in traffic control; hard real time is used in multimedia
In hard real time there is no room for delay; in soft real time a small delay can be tolerated
Hard real time allows long delays; soft real time allows none
There is no difference between them
mcqs.why: In hard real time, the work must be finished within the fixed time and there is no room for delay, such as a traffic control system; in soft real time, a small delay can be tolerated, such as online transactions and multimedia.

mcqs.q: A traffic control system is an example of which type of system?
mcqs.why: A traffic control system is the book's example of hard real time, where work must finish within the fixed time without delay.

mcqs.q: Online transactions and multimedia are examples of which type of system?
mcqs.why: Online transactions and multimedia are the book's examples of soft real time, where a small delay can be tolerated.

mcqs.q: In batch processing, jobs are processed…
options: in groups of similar jobs gathered in one batch
one user at a time only
within a fixed time without any delay
mcqs.why: Batch processing gathers similar jobs and runs them in one batch — the system divides similar jobs into groups.

mcqs.q: Windows 98 is an example of which type of operating system?
mcqs.why: The book gives DOS and Windows 98 as examples of single-user systems, in which only one user can work at a time.

mcqs.q: A real-time operating system must…
options: finish the work within the fixed time limit
mcqs.why: In a real-time system, work must be finished within the fixed time limit.

mcqs.q: According to the book's matching table, the real-time operating system is paired with which other type of operating system?
mcqs.why: As per the remaining pairing in the book's table, the real-time operating system is matched with the time-sharing operating system — both are types of operating systems.

mcqs.q: Why is a multi-user system useful where many people work together?
options: Many users can work at the same time and resources are shared
Only one user can work at a time
It finishes every job within a fixed time
It needs no resources at all
mcqs.why: In a multi-user system, many users can work at the same time and resources are shared — that is why it is better for an institution.

lessons.title: Office Automation and Antivirus Software
lessons.notes_html:
Office automation

Office automation is the group of programs that helps in the daily work of an office. Its purpose is to make the daily work of an office easy, fast and better. Its programs are linked with each other: for example, an Excel table can be brought into a Word document, and email can be sent through Outlook. MS Excel is an office automation program.

Programs in MS Office

ProgramUse
MS WordWriting documents
MS ExcelSpreadsheets and calculations
MS PowerPointPresentations
MS AccessDatabase management
MS OutlookEmail and contacts

Antivirus software

It is necessary to install antivirus software because it protects the computer from viruses, keeps data and the system safe from harm, and keeping its virus database updated also protects against new viruses.

mcqs.q: What is the group of programs that helps in the daily work of an office called?
mcqs.why: Office automation programs make the daily work of an office easier and better.

mcqs.q: Which statement correctly matches MS Excel?
options: It is the work the system is doing
It is an office automation program used for spreadsheets and calculations

mcqs.q: What is the purpose of office automation software?
options: To protect the computer from viruses
To run the hardware of the computer
To make the daily work of an office easy, fast and better
mcqs.why: The purpose of office automation is to make the daily work of an office easy, fast and better.

mcqs.q: How are office automation programs linked with each other?

They are never linked with each other
They are linked only through the printer

mcqs.why: MS PowerPoint is used for presentations; Word is for documents, Excel for spreadsheets, Access for databases and Outlook for email and contacts.

mcqs.q: Which MS Office program is used for email and contacts?
mcqs.why: MS Outlook is used for email and contacts, as listed in the book's MS Office programs.

mcqs.q: Why is it necessary to install antivirus software?
options: It protects the computer from viruses and keeps data and the system safe from harm
It makes the daily office work faster
It prepares the operating system in booting

mcqs.q: Keeping the antivirus virus database updated helps because…

it also protects against new viruses
it removes the need for an operating system
mcqs.why: Antivirus protects the computer from viruses, and keeping its virus database updated also protects against new viruses.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is NOT an office automation program?
mcqs.why: Word, Excel and PowerPoint are office automation programs in MS Office; the operating system is system software that runs the computer itself.

lessons.title: MS Word: Word Processing and Page Setup
lessons.notes_html:
What is a word processor?

A word processor is software with which documents are written, corrected and formatted. MS Word is the software used to write, correct and format a document — MS Word is commonly used for documentation.

Page orientation

  • Portrait: the page is taller than it is wide (upright page).
  • Landscape: the page is wider than it is tall (sideways page).

Margins and paper size — the Page Setup group

Margins fix the empty space (border) around the page; Size chooses the size of the page, such as A4 or Letter. Both options are found in the Page Setup group, which is used for margins, paper size and setting.

To set margins: in the Page Layout tab, click Margins and choose a ready-made margin, or write the top, bottom, left and right margin sizes yourself in Custom Margins.

mcqs.q: What is the software for formatting a document called?
mcqs.why: Word is used to write, correct and format documents.

mcqs.q: What is a word processor?
options: Software with which documents are written, corrected and formatted
mcqs.why: A word processor is software with which documents are written, corrected and formatted; its uses include writing letters and documents and making documents beautiful.

mcqs.q: Which statement correctly matches the common use of MS Word?
options: It arranges writing around a picture
It shows data in picture form
It puts data in a particular order
mcqs.why: MS Word is commonly used for making documents — documentation.

mcqs.q: What is portrait orientation?
options: The page is wider than it is tall (sideways page)
The page is taller than it is wide (upright page)
The page is divided into columns
mcqs.why: In portrait, the page is taller than it is wide (upright page); in landscape, the page is wider than it is tall.

mcqs.q: What is landscape orientation?
options: The page is taller than it is wide (upright page)
The page shows a faint picture behind the writing
The page holds a table of contents
The page is wider than it is tall (sideways page)
mcqs.why: In landscape, the page is wider than it is tall (sideways page); portrait is the upright page.

mcqs.q: How are margins set in a document?
options: In the Page Layout tab, click Margins and choose a ready-made margin, or write the sizes in Custom Margins
In the Home tab, click Bold
By changing the paper in the printer
mcqs.why: In the Page Layout tab, click Margins and choose a ready-made margin, or write the top, bottom, left and right margin sizes yourself in Custom Margins.

mcqs.q: What do margins fix in a document?
options: The empty space (border) around the page
mcqs.why: Margins fix the empty space (border) around the page; Size chooses the size of the page, such as A4 or Letter.

mcqs.q: Which statement correctly matches the Page Setup group?
options: It arranges writing around a picture
It is made on the basis of headings
It is for margins, paper size and setting
It shows data in picture form
mcqs.why: Margins, page size and orientation are fixed from the Page Setup group.

mcqs.q: A4 and Letter are examples of what in Page Setup?
mcqs.why: Size chooses the size of the page, such as A4 or Letter; both Size and Margins are found in the Page Setup group.

mcqs.q: Two uses of a word processor are…
options: writing letters and documents, and making documents beautiful by adding pictures, tables and colours
removing viruses and booting the computer
making databases and sending email only
mcqs.why: A word processor is used for writing letters and documents, and for making documents beautiful by adding pictures, tables and colours.

lessons.title: MS Word: Layout, Breaks, Columns and Objects
lessons.notes_html:
Themes and watermark

  • Themes change the overall design (the whole look) of a Word document with a set of colours, fonts and effects.
  • A watermark is faint writing or a picture appearing behind the writing on the page, which shows the status or ownership of the document. Examples: DRAFT, CONFIDENTIAL, a company logo.

Breaks

With a break, a new page or a new column is started in the document. A page break starts a new page, and a column break starts the writing in a new column.

Columns

The Columns option in the Page Setup group divides the writing into two or more columns, as in newspapers and magazines.

Arranging objects — the Arrange group

  • Position (Align Position) places a picture or object at a fixed place on the page.
  • Wrap Text arranges the writing around the picture.
  • Bring to Front / Bring Forward brings the selected object in front of the other objects; Send to Back / Send Backward sends the selected object behind the other objects. Both are used to order objects lying on top of each other.

mcqs.q: What is used to change the overall design of a Word document?
mcqs.why: Themes change the whole look of the document with a set of colours, fonts and effects.

mcqs.q: Which statement correctly matches Wrap Text?
options: It is made on the basis of headings
It is for margins, paper size and setting
Arranging the writing around the picture
mcqs.why: With Wrap Text, the writing wraps around the picture — it arranges the writing around the picture.

mcqs.q: What is a watermark in a document?
options: A dark line at the bottom of the page
The page number of the document
A table placed at the start of the document
Faint writing or a picture appearing behind the writing on the page, showing the status or ownership of the document
mcqs.why: A watermark is faint writing or a picture appearing behind the writing on the page, which shows the status or ownership of the document. Examples: DRAFT, CONFIDENTIAL, a company logo.

mcqs.q: DRAFT and CONFIDENTIAL are examples of what?
mcqs.why: DRAFT, CONFIDENTIAL and a company logo are the book's examples of watermarks — faint writing or a picture behind the writing on the page.

mcqs.q: What does a page break do in a document?
options: It starts the writing in a new column
It joins two pages into one
mcqs.why: With a break, a new page or a new column is started: a page break starts a new page, and a column break starts the writing in a new column.

mcqs.q: What does a column break do?
options: It starts the writing in a new column
mcqs.why: A column break starts the writing in a new column; a page break starts a new page.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between Send to Back and Bring to Front?
options: Both bring the object to the front
Both send the object to the back
They change the size of the object
Bring Forward brings the selected object in front of the others; Send Backward sends it behind the others
mcqs.why: Bring Forward brings the selected object in front of the other objects; Send Backward sends the selected object behind the other objects. Both order objects lying on top of each other.

mcqs.q: The Columns option in the Page Setup group…
options: divides the writing into two or more columns, as in newspapers and magazines
removes all columns from the page
changes the colour of the writing
fixes the margins of the page
mcqs.why: The Columns option divides the writing into two or more columns, as in newspapers and magazines.

mcqs.q: What does the Position option do with a picture or object?
options: It arranges the writing around it
It places it at a fixed place on the page
It deletes it from the page
mcqs.why: Position places a picture or object at a fixed place on the page; Wrap Text arranges the writing around the picture.

mcqs.q: Themes change the look of a document through a set of…
mcqs.why: Themes change the whole look of the document with a set of colours, fonts and effects.

lessons.title: Table of Contents in MS Word
lessons.notes_html:
What is a Table of Contents (ToC)?

A table of contents holds a list of headings and their pages, so the reader can quickly find the wanted topic and reach that page directly.

Making a ToC effective

  • The most important thing for making a table of contents effective is page numbering — having the correct page number with every heading, so that the reader can quickly find the wanted topic.
  • An automatic table of contents is made on the basis of headings — it is made by itself from the headings of the document.

mcqs.q: What is the most important thing for making a table of contents effective?
mcqs.why: In a table of contents, having the correct page number with every heading is most important, so that the reader can quickly find the wanted topic.

mcqs.q: Which statement correctly matches an automatic table of contents?
options: It is made on the basis of headings
Arranging the writing around the picture
It is for margins, paper size and setting
mcqs.why: An automatic table of contents is made by itself from the headings of the document.

mcqs.q: How does a Table of Contents (ToC) help the reader?
options: It makes the document's pages colourful
It holds a list of headings and their pages, so the reader can quickly find the wanted topic and reach that page directly
It checks the spelling of the document
mcqs.why: A table of contents holds a list of headings and their pages, so the reader can quickly find the wanted topic and reach that page directly.

mcqs.q: A table of contents contains…
options: the full text of every chapter
a list of headings with their page numbers
a list of difficult words and their meanings
mcqs.why: A table of contents holds a list of headings and their pages — the correct page number with every heading is what makes it effective.

mcqs.q: Why must the page number with every heading in a ToC be correct?
options: So that the document looks longer
So that the headings become bold
So that the pages print in colour
So that the reader can quickly find the wanted topic

mcqs.q: An automatic ToC is prepared from which part of the document?

mcqs.why: An automatic table is made on the basis of headings — it is made by itself from the headings of the document.

mcqs.q: If a reader wants to reach a topic's page directly, which part of the document helps most?
mcqs.why: The table of contents holds the headings and their pages, so the reader can reach the wanted page directly.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is NOT a part of a table of contents?

mcqs.why: A table of contents holds only a list of headings and their pages; the full text of the lessons is in the document itself.

mcqs.q: The effectiveness of a ToC depends most on…
options: correct page numbering with every heading
mcqs.why: Having the correct page number with every heading is most important for making a table of contents effective.

mcqs.q: A table of contents is usually placed…
options: with the list of headings and pages for the whole document
inside a picture on the page
behind the writing as a watermark
only in the Page Setup group
mcqs.why: A table of contents holds a list of headings and their pages for the document, helping the reader find topics quickly.

lessons.title: MS Excel: Formulas and Calculations
lessons.notes_html:
MS Excel

MS Excel is used for calculations, spreadsheets and formulas. Excel organises, displays, formats and calculates data.

Formulas

  • Every formula in Excel starts with the equals sign (=).
  • Total of marks in cells B2 to E2: =Sum(B2 to E2) — the total marks are the sum of the four subjects' marks, which Sum gives.
  • Percentage of marks out of 400: =(B2+C2+D2+E2)/400*100 — the obtained marks are divided by the total 400 and multiplied by 100. (In the book's printed question the options contain an error: two options are printed identically and none is mathematically correct; the formula given here is the correct one.)
  • To multiply 37 by 15, write in the formula bar: =37*15 — start with =, write 37, the multiplication sign (*) and 15, then press Enter; the answer 555 will come.

mcqs.q: Which software is used for calculations?
mcqs.why: Excel is used for calculations, spreadsheets and formulas.

mcqs.q: Which sign is used to start a formula in Excel?
mcqs.why: Every formula in Excel starts with the equals sign (=).

mcqs.q: Which is the correct formula to find the total marks in the given table (marks in B2, C2, D2 and E2)?
mcqs.why: The total marks are the sum of the four subjects' marks, which =Sum(B2 to E2) gives.

mcqs.q: Which is the correct formula to find the percentage of marks out of a total of 400?
mcqs.why: The obtained marks are divided by the total 400 and multiplied by 100: =(B2+C2+D2+E2)/400*100. Note: the book's printed options for this question contain an error — two options are printed identically and none is mathematically correct.

mcqs.q: What must be written in the MS Excel formula bar to multiply 37 by 15?
mcqs.why: Write =37*15 — start with the equals sign, write 37, the multiplication sign (*) and 15, then press Enter; the answer 555 will come.

mcqs.q: What is the answer of the Excel formula =37*15?
mcqs.why: =37*15 gives 555 — 37 multiplied by 15 — when the formula is written in the formula bar and Enter is pressed.

mcqs.q: Which statement correctly matches the use of Excel?
options: Arranging the writing around the picture
Organising, displaying, formatting and calculating data

mcqs.q: In Excel, the Sum function is used to…
options: add the values of cells together
mcqs.why: The total marks are the sum of the four subjects' marks, which the Sum function gives — for example =Sum(B2 to E2).

mcqs.q: To find a percentage in Excel, the obtained marks are…
options: multiplied by the total marks and divided by 100
divided by the total marks and multiplied by 100
mcqs.why: The correct formula is =(B2+C2+D2+E2)/400*100 — the obtained marks are divided by the total 400 and multiplied by 100.

mcqs.q: Which symbol is used for multiplication inside an Excel formula?
mcqs.why: In =37*15, the multiplication sign (*) multiplies 37 by 15; every formula begins with the equals sign.

mcqs.q: A formula in Excel always begins with…
options: the name of the function only
mcqs.why: Every formula starts with the equals sign (=) — for example =37*15 or =Sum(B2 to E2).

mcqs.q: Which program would you use to keep marks in a table and calculate totals and percentages?
mcqs.why: Excel is used for calculations, spreadsheets and formulas — it organises, displays, formats and calculates data such as marks, totals and percentages.

mcqs.q: In the formula =Sum(B2 to E2), B2 to E2 stands for…
options: the four cells holding the four subjects' marks
the page numbers of the document
the names of four students only
mcqs.why: B2 to E2 are the cells holding the four subjects' marks; their sum gives the total marks.

mcqs.q: What happens after writing =37*15 in the formula bar and pressing Enter?
mcqs.why: Start with the equals sign, write 37, the multiplication sign (*) and 15, then press Enter; the answer 555 will come.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a correct Excel formula?
mcqs.why: =Sum(B2 to E2) is the correct formula for the total marks — every Excel formula starts with the equals sign.

lessons.title: Sorting, Charts and the Uses of Spreadsheets
lessons.notes_html:
Sorting

Sorting is the function that puts data in a particular order — it puts data in alphabetical or numerical order.

Charts

Charts are basically used for showing data in picture form — a chart gives data a pictorial expression so that it is easy to understand.

  • Pie chart: shows the parts of a total — the shares of three business partners show best in a pie chart.
  • The book also names line, bar and area charts.

Uses of spreadsheets in business

In business, spreadsheets are used to keep accounts, budgets, salaries, stock and sales records, and profit-and-loss calculations.

Kind of hitCountRunsShare of 149 runs
Ones (1s)2121 × 1 = 2121/149 × 100 = 14.09%
