chapters.title: Unit 4: Data Communication and Computer Networks

lessons.title: The Communication System and Its Qualities
lessons.notes_html:
Parts of a communication system

A communication system is made of five parts:

PartMeaning
MessageThe information sent
SenderThe device that sends the message
ReceiverThe device that receives the message
MediumThe path, such as a wire or radio waves
ProtocolThe rules

Example: in sending an email, the writing is the message, the computers are the sender and receiver, the internet is the medium, and the email rules are the protocol.

Qualities of a good communication system

  • Delivery: the data must reach the correct destination, not some other place.
  • Accuracy
  • Timeliness

Addresses and bit rate

Both the physical and logical addresses of every device are unique — each device has its own address. The bit rate is measured in bits per second (bps); examples: kilobits per second (Kbps) and megabits per second (Mbps).

mcqs.q: Of how many parts is a communication system made?
mcqs.why: A communication system has five parts: message, sender, receiver, medium and protocol.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is a part of a communication system?
mcqs.why: The five parts of a communication system are the message, sender, receiver, medium and protocol (the rules).

mcqs.q: What are both the physical and logical addresses of a device?
mcqs.why: Every device's physical and logical address is its own unique address.

mcqs.q: In sending an email, what is the medium?
mcqs.why: In the book's email example, the writing is the message, the computers are the sender and receiver, the internet is the medium, and the email rules are the protocol.

mcqs.q: In the email example, the writing itself is which part of the communication system?
mcqs.why: In sending an email, the writing is the message — the information sent.

mcqs.q: What are the three basic qualities of a good communication system?
mcqs.why: A good communication system has three basic qualities: delivery, accuracy and timeliness.

mcqs.q: In a good communication system, 'delivery' means…
options: the data must be printed at once
the data must be deleted after sending
the data must reach the correct destination, not some other place
the data must reach every device on the network
mcqs.why: Delivery means that the data must reach the correct destination, not some other place — one of the three qualities of a good communication system.

mcqs.q: In which unit is the bit rate measured?
mcqs.why: The bit rate is measured in bits per second (bps); examples are kilobits per second (Kbps) and megabits per second (Mbps).

mcqs.q: Kbps and Mbps are examples of units of…
mcqs.why: The bit rate is measured in bits per second (bps); kilobits per second (Kbps) and megabits per second (Mbps) are its examples.

mcqs.q: The rules followed in communication are called the…
mcqs.why: The protocol is the set of rules in a communication system — for example, the email rules in sending an email.

lessons.title: Transmission Media and Signal Problems
lessons.notes_html:
Guided and unguided media

Wired media is called guided media, because the signal travels along the path of the wire.

CablePrice / installationData rateInterference
Twisted pair (UTP)Cheap and easy to installLowMore interference
STPShieldedFaster than UTPLess interference because of the shield
Coaxial cableUsed in cable TVHigher than twisted pairLess interference
Fibre opticExpensiveThe highest — signal travels by lightThe least interference

Layers of a coaxial cable: a copper wire in the middle, a plastic core (insulation) around it, a mesh of metal wires (shield) outside that, and a plastic cover outermost.

Radio waves and microwaves

  • Radio waves: low frequency, can pass through obstacles and spread in all directions; used in AM/FM radio, TV and cordless phones.
  • Microwaves: higher frequency, need a line-of-sight path; used in mobile phones, satellites and terrestrial links.

Signal impairment

  • Attenuation: the weakening of the signal during its journey; it is treated with an amplifier.
  • Distortion: a change in the shape of the signal between sender and receiver.
  • Noise: unwanted signals mixing in.

Modulation is changing a digital signal into an analogue signal.

Connections through telephone lines

  • Dial-up modem: slow connection through the telephone line.
  • DSL modem: fast connection through the telephone line.
  • ISDN modem: voice, data and video through a digital network.

mcqs.q: What is wired media called?
mcqs.why: Wired media is called guided media, because the signal travels along the path of the wire.

mcqs.q: What is it called when the shape of the signal changes between sender and receiver?
mcqs.why: In distortion, the shape of the signal changes during its journey.

mcqs.q: What is the weakening of a signal during transmission called?
mcqs.why: In attenuation, the signal becomes weak during its journey.

mcqs.q: Which statement correctly matches a difference in the shape of the signal?
mcqs.why: A difference coming in the shape of the signal is called distortion — one of the three causes of signal impairment.

mcqs.q: What are the three causes of signal impairment?
mcqs.why: There are three causes of signal impairment: attenuation (weakening of the signal), distortion (change in the shape of the signal) and noise (unwanted signals mixing in).

mcqs.q: Attenuation of a signal is treated with which device?
mcqs.why: In attenuation, the signal becomes weak during its journey, and it is treated with an amplifier, which strengthens the weak signal.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between radio waves and microwaves?
options: Radio waves are of low frequency and pass through obstacles; microwaves are of higher frequency and need a line-of-sight path
Radio waves need line of sight; microwaves pass through walls
Microwaves are used only in radio and TV
mcqs.why: Radio waves are of low frequency, can pass through obstacles and spread in all directions; microwaves are of higher frequency and need a line-of-sight path.

mcqs.q: Radio waves are used in which of the following?
options: AM/FM radio, TV and cordless phones
mcqs.why: Radio waves are used in AM/FM radio, TV and cordless phones; microwaves are used in mobile phones, satellites and terrestrial links.

mcqs.q: Microwaves are used in which of the following?
options: Mobile phones, satellites and terrestrial links
mcqs.why: Microwaves are of higher frequency, need a line-of-sight path, and are used in mobile phones, satellites and terrestrial links.

mcqs.q: What is changing a digital signal into an analogue signal called?
mcqs.why: In modulation, a digital signal is changed into an analogue signal.

mcqs.q: Which cable carries the signal by light and gives the highest data rate?
mcqs.why: In fibre optic, the signal travels by light; it has the highest data rate and the least interference, but it is expensive.

mcqs.q: UTP cable is cheap and easy to install, but it has…
options: a low data rate and more interference
mcqs.why: Twisted pair (UTP) is cheap and easy to install, but has a low data rate and more interference.

mcqs.q: Why does STP cable have less interference than UTP?
mcqs.why: STP has less interference because of the shield, and a faster data rate than UTP.

mcqs.q: In a coaxial cable, the innermost part is…
mcqs.why: In a coaxial cable there is a copper wire in the middle, a plastic core (insulation) around it, a mesh of metal wires (shield) outside that, and a plastic cover outermost.

mcqs.q: Which connection through a telephone line gives voice, data and video through a digital network?
mcqs.why: Dial-up is a slow connection through the telephone line, DSL is a fast connection through the telephone line, and ISDN gives voice, data and video through a digital network.

lessons.title: Networks, Topologies and Network Devices
lessons.notes_html:
LAN, MAN and WAN — examples

  • LAN: a school or office network.
  • MAN: a city's cable TV network.
  • WAN: the internet — a WAN joins many networks with each other over a large area.

Topologies: advantage and disadvantage

TopologyAdvantageDisadvantage
BusCheap and easyIf the central cable breaks, the whole network stops
RingEvery computer gets the signal in turnIf one computer fails, the whole network stops
StarEasy to set up; one computer's failure does not affect the othersIf the hub fails, the whole network stops; more cable is needed

In star topology, all computers are joined to a central hub or switch.

Hardware needed for each topology

  • Bus: central cable, terminators, NIC, connectors.
  • Ring: cable, NIC.
  • Star: hub or switch, cables, NIC.

In every topology, an NIC is needed to join the computers to the network.

Network devices

DeviceWork
AmplifierStrengthens a weak signal
RouterJoins two or more networks and chooses the best and shortest route for data
SwitchJoins the devices of a network (computers, printers) with each other
HubJoins many computers in one network

mcqs.q: Which topology is it in which all computers are joined to a central hub?
mcqs.why: In star topology, all computers are joined to a central hub or switch.

mcqs.q: By which route does a router send data packets?
mcqs.why: A router chooses the best and shortest route for the data.

mcqs.q: What is the work of a router?
options: It joins many computers in one network only
It joins two or more networks and chooses the best route for data
mcqs.why: A router joins two or more networks and chooses the best route for data; an amplifier strengthens a weak signal and a hub joins many computers in one network.

mcqs.q: Which device strengthens a weak signal?
mcqs.why: An amplifier strengthens a weak signal — it is the treatment for attenuation.

mcqs.q: Which device joins the devices of a network (computers, printers) with each other?
mcqs.why: A switch joins the devices of a network (computers, printers) with each other.

mcqs.q: A hub is a device that…
options: chooses the best route between networks
joins many computers in one network
mcqs.why: A hub is a device that joins many computers in one network.

mcqs.q: What is the disadvantage of bus topology?
options: If the hub fails, the network stops
It needs the most cable of all
Only one computer can be joined
If the central cable breaks, the whole network stops
mcqs.why: Bus topology is cheap and easy, but if the central cable breaks, the whole network stops.

mcqs.q: In ring topology, what happens if one computer fails?
mcqs.why: In ring topology every computer gets the signal in turn, but if one computer fails, the whole network stops.

mcqs.q: What is the main disadvantage of star topology?
options: If one computer fails, the whole network stops
If the hub fails, the whole network stops, and more cable is needed
It is very cheap and easy
mcqs.why: Star topology is easy to set up and one computer's failure does not affect the others, but if the hub fails, the whole network stops, and more cable is needed.

mcqs.q: A school or office network is an example of which network?
mcqs.why: LAN: a school or office network; MAN: a city's cable TV network; WAN: the internet.

mcqs.q: A city's cable TV network is an example of which network?
mcqs.why: A MAN covers a city — the book's example is a city's cable TV network.

mcqs.q: The internet is an example of which network?
mcqs.why: The internet is a WAN — a WAN joins many networks with each other over a large area.

mcqs.q: Which statement correctly matches networking that joins two networks over a large area?
mcqs.why: A WAN joins many networks with each other over a large area — as per the pairing in the book's table.

mcqs.q: Which hardware is needed in every topology to join computers to the network?
mcqs.why: Bus needs cable, terminators, NIC and connectors; ring needs cable and NIC; star needs a hub or switch, cables and NIC. In every topology, an NIC is needed.

mcqs.q: Which hardware list belongs to star topology?
mcqs.why: Star topology needs a hub or switch, cables and an NIC; bus needs the central cable, terminators, NIC and connectors; ring needs cable and NIC.

lessons.title: The OSI Model, Standards and Addresses
lessons.notes_html:
The OSI model

The OSI model is divided into seven layers (bottom to top):

  1. Physical
  2. Data Link
  3. Network
  4. Transport
  5. Session
  6. Presentation
  7. Application

To remember: All People Seem To Need Data Processing.

  • The physical (MAC) address is used at the data link layer.
  • The network layer fixes the route of the data, and the route can change if needed.
  • TCP and UDP are protocols of the transport layer.

IP addresses

An IPv4 address uses 32 bits (4 bytes). An IPv4 address has two parts: the network part and the host (device) part.

Standardisation organisations

The purpose of standardisation organisations is to make common standards and rules so that the devices and systems of different companies can work with each other. Examples: ISO, IEEE, IETF, ITU and ANSI. IEEE is the international organisation of electrical and electronics engineering.

mcqs.q: Which is the organisation of electrical and electronics engineers?
mcqs.why: IEEE is the international organisation of electrical and electronics engineering.

mcqs.q: How many bits are used in an IPv4 address?
mcqs.why: An IPv4 address is 32 bits (4 bytes), as given in the book's exercise on data communication.

mcqs.q: Into how many layers is the OSI model divided?
mcqs.why: The OSI model is divided into seven layers: Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation, Application.

mcqs.q: Which is the correct order of the OSI layers from bottom to top?
options: Application, Presentation, Session, Transport, Network, Data Link, Physical
Physical, Network, Data Link, Transport, Application, Session, Presentation
Data Link, Physical, Transport, Network, Session, Application, Presentation
Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation, Application
mcqs.why: The seven layers from bottom to top are: Physical, Data Link, Network, Transport, Session, Presentation, Application — 'All People Seem To Need Data Processing'.

mcqs.q: Which sentence helps to remember the OSI layers?
options: All People Seem To Need Data Processing
Please Do Not Throw Sausage Pizza Away
mcqs.why: The book gives 'All People Seem To Need Data Processing' to remember the OSI layers from bottom to top.

mcqs.q: Which statement correctly matches the parts of an IPv4 address?
mcqs.why: An IPv4 address has two parts: the network part and the host (device) part.

mcqs.q: Which statement correctly matches the physical address?
options: It is used at the transport layer
It is used at the application layer
It is used at the data link layer
It fixes the route of the data
mcqs.why: The physical (MAC) address is used at the data link layer.

mcqs.q: Which statement correctly matches the use of TCP and UDP?
options: They are used at the data link layer
They fix the route of the data
They are parts of an IPv4 address
They are protocols of the transport layer
mcqs.why: TCP and UDP are protocols of the transport layer.

mcqs.q: Which OSI layer fixes the route of the data?
options: Network layer — and the route can change if needed
mcqs.why: The network layer fixes the route of the data, and the route can change if needed — as per the book's matching exercise.

mcqs.q: What is the purpose of standardisation organisations?
options: To sell computers to all companies
To make common standards and rules so that the devices and systems of different companies can work with each other
To give internet connections to homes
mcqs.why: The purpose of standardisation organisations is to make common standards and rules so that the devices and systems of different companies can work with each other. Examples: ISO, IEEE, IETF, ITU and ANSI.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is a standardisation organisation?
mcqs.why: ISO, IEEE, IETF, ITU and ANSI are standardisation organisations that make common standards and rules.

mcqs.q: An IPv4 address of 32 bits is equal to how many bytes?
mcqs.why: An IPv4 address is 32 bits, which is 4 bytes — 8 bits make one byte, so 32 bits make 4 bytes.

mcqs.q: The host part of an IPv4 address identifies…
mcqs.why: An IPv4 address has two parts: the network part and the host (device) part.

mcqs.q: At which layer is the physical (MAC) address used?
mcqs.why: The physical (MAC) address is used at the data link layer, as given in the book.

mcqs.q: TCP and UDP work at which layer of the OSI model?
mcqs.why: TCP and UDP are protocols of the transport layer.

lessons.title: Malware: Virus, Worm, Adware and Spyware
lessons.notes_html:
Malware

Malware is the broad term that includes different harmful software — virus, worm, spyware and adware.

The four kinds compared

MalwareLevel of dangerHow it startsDamage / effectSource of spread
VirusMedium-highStarts by opening an infected fileDamages files; slows the computerInfected files, email and USB
WormHighStarts by itself through the network; not attached to any fileDamages the system; slows the computer a lotNetwork / internet
AdwareLowComes with free software and advertisementsLittle damage; slows the systemAdvertisements and free software
SpywareHighComes hidden in a downloadSteals information; slows the computerInfected websites and downloads
  • Adware is the advertising software that uses pop-up windows. It does not copy or steal data, and so is the least harmful malware.
  • A worm copies itself by itself and is not attached to any file.
  • Sources of virus spread: email attachment, internet download, flash disk/CD. According to the book, the most famous source is the email attachment.

mcqs.q: What is the broad term that includes different harmful software?
mcqs.why: Malware is the broad term that includes virus, worm, spyware and adware.

mcqs.q: Which malware does not copy or steal data, and so is the least harmful?
mcqs.why: Adware only shows advertisements and does not steal data, so it is the least harmful.

mcqs.q: Which malware copies itself by itself and is not attached to any file?
mcqs.why: A worm copies itself by itself, spreads through the network, and is not attached to any file.

mcqs.q: Which statement correctly matches the advertising software that uses pop-up windows?
mcqs.why: Adware is advertising software that shows advertisements in pop-up windows.

mcqs.q: According to the book, what is the most famous source of the spread of a virus?
mcqs.why: A virus spreads through email attachment, internet download and flash disk/CD; according to the book, the most famous source is email attachment. (Note: in the printed question all four options are real sources of virus spread.)

mcqs.q: Which malware steals information and comes hidden in a download?
mcqs.why: Spyware comes hidden in a download, steals information and slows the computer; its danger level is high.

mcqs.q: Which malware starts by opening an infected file and damages files?
mcqs.why: A virus starts by opening an infected file, damages files, slows the computer, and spreads through infected files, email and USB.

mcqs.q: Which malware has a high danger level and spreads by itself through the network?
mcqs.why: A worm has a high danger level; it starts by itself through the network, damages the system and slows the computer a lot.

mcqs.q: Adware usually comes with…
mcqs.why: Adware comes with free software and advertisements; it does little damage and is the least harmful malware.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is a source of virus spread?
mcqs.why: A virus spreads through email attachment, internet download and flash disk/CD.

mcqs.q: Spyware spreads through…
mcqs.why: Spyware spreads through infected websites and downloads, and it steals information.

mcqs.q: Which malware slows the computer a lot?
options: All malware speed up the computer
mcqs.why: A worm damages the system and slows the computer a lot; a virus and spyware also slow the computer, and adware slows the system a little.

mcqs.q: Malware includes which of the following?
mcqs.why: Malware is the broad term that includes virus, worm, spyware and adware.

mcqs.q: Which malware is attached to a file and needs that file to be opened?
mcqs.why: A virus starts by opening an infected file; a worm is different — it copies itself by itself and is not attached to any file.

mcqs.q: A flash disk or CD can be a source of the spread of…
mcqs.why: A virus spreads through infected files, email and USB flash disk/CD.

lessons.title: Security, Authentication and Hacking
lessons.notes_html:
Why computer security is important

  • Computer security protects hardware, software and information from theft and damage.
  • Personal information (passwords, bank details, pictures) stays safe.
  • The system keeps working correctly.
  • Business and government work depend on the protection of information.

Authentication

The purpose of authentication of information is to make sure that only the right person can reach the data or system, no one else. Authentication methods in the book include username-password, scan code, biometric and PIN. In biometrics, a person is verified by their own bodily identity (fingerprints, eye) — it identifies only the real user. The PIN is the secret code (personal identification number) that identifies the user.

Hacking

  • Ethical hacking: the weaknesses of a system or network are found with permission and fixed. An ethical hacker is also called a white-hat hacker.
  • Cracker: the person who enters someone's computer by bypassing the password (illegally).

Protection

Antivirus software saves data and the system from the damage of viruses and malware.

Steps to save an email account from hacking

  • Keep a strong password.
  • Do not share the password with anyone.
  • Do not click unknown links or attachments.
  • Keep the antivirus updated.
  • Log out on a shared computer.

mcqs.q: Which authentication method identifies only the real user?
mcqs.why: In biometrics, a person is verified by their own bodily identity (fingerprints, eye), so it identifies only the real user.

mcqs.q: Why is computer security important?
options: It increases the size of the screen
It removes the need for passwords
It protects hardware, software and information from theft and damage
mcqs.why: Computer security protects hardware, software and information from theft and damage; personal information stays safe and the system keeps working correctly.

mcqs.q: What is the purpose of authentication of information?
options: To make sure that only the right person can reach the data or system, no one else
To make data reach every user
mcqs.why: The purpose of authentication is to make sure that only the right person can reach the data or system, no one else.

mcqs.q: What is ethical hacking?
options: Entering someone's computer by bypassing the password
Finding the weaknesses of a system or network with permission and fixing them
mcqs.why: In ethical hacking, the weaknesses of a system or network are found with permission and fixed. An ethical hacker is also called a white-hat hacker.

mcqs.q: An ethical hacker is also called a…
mcqs.why: An ethical hacker — who finds weaknesses with permission and fixes them — is also called a white-hat hacker.

mcqs.q: Which statement correctly matches the secret code that identifies the user?
mcqs.why: The PIN is that personal identification number which identifies the user.

mcqs.q: Which statement correctly matches the person who enters someone's computer by bypassing the password?
mcqs.why: A cracker is the person who enters someone's system illegally by bypassing the password.

mcqs.q: Which statement correctly matches the software that saves data from damage?
mcqs.why: Antivirus software saves data and the system from the damage of viruses and malware.

mcqs.q: Which step helps to save an email account from hacking?
options: Share the password with close friends
Keep a strong password and do not share it with anyone
mcqs.why: To save an email account: keep a strong password, do not share the password with anyone, do not click unknown links or attachments, keep the antivirus updated, and log out on a shared computer.

mcqs.q: Why should you log out of your account on a shared computer?
options: So that no one else can reach your data or system
mcqs.why: Logging out on a shared computer is one of the steps to save an email account from hacking, so that only the right person can reach the account.

lessons.title: Cybercrime and Online Safety
lessons.notes_html:
Cybercrime

A crime done through a computer or network is called cybercrime.

Common online dangers

  • Cyberbullying: someone is threatened, teased or defamed through a computer, mobile or the internet. Example: spreading false talk about a student on social media, or sending them insulting messages.
  • Phishing: a false email or website asking for bank details or a password; a false message luring with a prize; a false login page that steals the password.
  • Clickjacking: according to the book, making someone click by the lure of a prize — e.g. "Click the link, get 5 dollars of mobile balance".
  • Scam / fraud: demanding an advance fee by the lure of a prize.

What to do

  • If a friend becomes a victim of cyber harassment: do not answer the harasser, keep the evidence safe (screenshots), block them, tell parents or a teacher, and report to the National Response Centre for Cyber Crime (helpline 9911).
  • Prize on the phone with an advance fee demanded: do not pay the fee and end the call.
  • Unknown email demanding a bank or email password: do not reply and do not tell the password — it is phishing.
  • Unknown website demanding Facebook or Google account details: do not write the details and close the site.

mcqs.q: "Click the link, get 5 dollars of mobile balance" — what is this an example of?
mcqs.why: According to the book, making someone click by the lure of a prize is clickjacking.

mcqs.q: Which statement correctly matches the name of a crime done through a computer system?
mcqs.why: A crime done through a computer or network is called cybercrime.

mcqs.q: What is cyberbullying?
options: Entering a system with permission to fix it
Threatening, teasing or defaming someone through a computer, mobile or the internet
mcqs.why: In cyberbullying, someone is threatened, teased or defamed through a computer, mobile or the internet — for example, spreading false talk about a student on social media.

mcqs.q: Your friend has become a victim of cyber harassment. What is the best advice?
options: Answer the harasser in the same way
Delete all the evidence at once
Share the harasser's messages with everyone
Do not answer the harasser, keep the evidence safe, block them, tell parents or a teacher, and report it
mcqs.why: Do not answer the harasser, keep the evidence safe (screenshots), block them, tell parents or a teacher, and report to the National Response Centre for Cyber Crime (helpline 9911).

mcqs.q: Cyber harassment in Pakistan can be reported to the National Response Centre for Cyber Crime on helpline…
mcqs.why: The book gives the National Response Centre for Cyber Crime helpline 9911 for reporting cyber harassment.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is an example of phishing?
options: A student teased on social media
A false email or website asking for bank details or a password
mcqs.why: Phishing examples: a false email or website asking for bank details or a password; a false message luring with a prize; a false login page that steals the password.

mcqs.q: A false login page that steals the password is an example of…
mcqs.why: A false login page that steals the password is one of the book's examples of phishing.

mcqs.q: Someone is told of a prize on the phone and an advance fee is demanded. What should be done?
options: Pay a small fee at once
Ask them to send the prize first and pay later
Do not pay the fee and end the call
mcqs.why: Do not pay the fee and end the call — demanding an advance fee by the lure of a prize is fraud/scam.

mcqs.q: An unknown email demands your bank account or email password. What should be done?
options: Do not reply and do not tell the password
Click the link in the email
mcqs.why: Do not reply and do not tell the password — demanding personal information in an unknown email is phishing.

mcqs.q: An unknown website demands your Facebook or Google account details. What should be done?
options: Do not write the details and close the site
Save the password on the site
mcqs.why: Do not write the details and close the site — demanding account details on an unknown website can lead to theft of information.

mcqs.q: Spreading false talk about a student on social media is an example of…
mcqs.why: Spreading false talk about a student on social media, or sending insulting messages, is the book's example of cyberbullying.

mcqs.q: Making someone click a link by the lure of a prize is called…
mcqs.why: According to the book, making someone click by the lure of a prize is clickjacking.

mcqs.q: Demanding an advance fee by the lure of a prize is…
mcqs.why: Demanding an advance fee by the lure of a prize is fraud/scam — do not pay the fee and end the call.

mcqs.q: If you receive insulting messages online, the evidence should be…
mcqs.why: A victim of cyber harassment should keep the evidence safe (screenshots), block the harasser and report the matter.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a cybercrime?
options: Stealing a password through a false login page
Logging out of a shared computer
mcqs.why: Stealing a password through a false login page is phishing — a crime done through a computer or network, which is called cybercrime.

lessons.title: Ethics, Copyright and Software Piracy
lessons.notes_html:
Copyright

Copyright is the legal right that keeps a person's own creation (book, software, writing, art) safe — another person cannot copy or use it without permission. Software is mostly protected under copyright law. Copying some material from the internet without giving reference to its real owner is a copyright violation.

Plagiarism

Presenting someone else's ideas or writing as one's own (under one's own name) is plagiarism.

Professional ethics

Professional ethics in computers are important because ethics create a positive and healthy work environment — a work place of honesty, respect and responsibility. (Note: the book's printed options for this question contain an error; the intended answer is that ethics create a positive and healthy work environment.)

Free antivirus

A free antivirus mostly gives only limited service — it does not have all the facilities.

Software piracy

Software piracy is harmful for a software developer: through piracy, the developer does not get the income of their hard work, the money for research on new software becomes less, and jobs are affected.

Poster on the safe use of computers and the internet

Points to include: save your computer from viruses; avoid cyberbullying; avoid plagiarism; stay aware of cybercrime.

mcqs.why: Software is mostly protected under copyright law.

mcqs.why: Using someone's material by copying it without permission is a copyright violation.

mcqs.why: A free antivirus does not have all the facilities — it gives only limited service.

mcqs.why: Through piracy, the developer does not get the income of their hard work, the money for research on new software becomes less, and jobs are affected.

ethics create a positive and healthy work environment
mcqs.why: Professional ethics make a work place of honesty, respect and responsibility — they create a positive and healthy work environment. (The book's printed options contain an error; this is the intended answer.)

mcqs.q: Professional ethics make a workplace of…

lessons.title: Websites, Hosting and Browsers
lessons.notes_html:
The web server and web hosting

  • A web server is the computer that keeps the website's files safe and delivers them to the users — it is responsible for public access to a website.
  • Web hosting is the service that places a website on the internet so that all people can reach it.

Kinds of websites

  • Forum site: users can ask questions and talk on different topics.
  • News website: delivers fresh news, weather and current affairs.
  • Social site and blog site are also named in the book.
  • E-commerce: business done through the internet — a business website.

The web browser and HTML

A web browser converts HTML code, by which the document (web page) appears.

Steps in making a complete website

  1. Open a text editor.
  2. Write the HTML code.
  3. Save the file with the .html extension.
  4. View it in the browser.
  5. For a complete site, make all the pages, join them with links, and publish them on hosting.

Text editors and web designing tools

Notepad, Microsoft FrontPage, Adobe Dreamweaver, WordPress, Wix, Microsoft Visual Studio, Adobe XD.

mcqs.q: Which service is responsible for public access to a website?
mcqs.why: A web server is the computer that delivers the website's content to the users.

mcqs.q: Which specific kind of website is it where users can ask questions and talk on different topics?
mcqs.why: On a forum site, users can ask questions and talk on different topics.

mcqs.q: A news website is specific for delivering which information?
mcqs.why: A news site delivers fresh news, weather and current affairs.

mcqs.q: Which code does a web browser convert, by which the document appears?
mcqs.why: The browser reads HTML code and shows it in the form of a web page.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between web hosting and a web server?
options: A web server is a service; hosting is a computer
Web hosting is the service that places a website on the internet; a web server is the computer that keeps the website's files and delivers them to users
Hosting delivers files; the server places the site on the internet

lessons.title: Lists, Links and Images in HTML
lessons.notes_html:
Lists

  • Ordered list (<ol>): items are shown in the order of numbers or letters.
  • Unordered list (<ul>): items are shown with bullets, without any order.
  • The <ul>, <ol> and <dl> tags arrange information in the form of lists.

Links

A link is made with the <a href="..."> tag (anchor). Example: <a href="http://www.google.com">Goto Google</a> — clicking on it takes the user to the other page. A hyperlink adds navigation support in web pages: with it, the user can go from one page to another page.

Images

Pictures are shown with the <img> tag, in which the address of the picture is written in src. Example: <img src="bridge.jpg" alt="Bridge" width="600">. <img> is an empty tag; it does not need to be closed. With the <img> tag, pictures and infographics are added on the web page.

mcqs.q: Which kind of list shows the items in numbers or order?

mcqs.q: Which tag is used to join (link) to another page?

mcqs.q: Tell the difference between ordered and unordered lists.

mcqs.q: Which statement correctly matches the <ul>, <ol> and <dl> tags?

mcqs.q: Which statement correctly matches the <img> tag?

mcqs.why: The <a> tag makes a hyperlink with href — for example <a href="http://www.google.com">Goto Google</a>.

mcqs.why: In an unordered list (<ul>), items are shown with bullets, without any order.

lessons.title: Tables and Frames in HTML
lessons.notes_html:
Table elements

ElementWork
<table>Makes a table — arranges information in rows and columns
<tr>Makes a row
<td>Makes a data cell

lessons.title: Data, Databases and DBMS
lessons.notes_html:
Data and database

  • Data are simple facts that have not been arranged.
  • A table is one set of arranged rows and columns about one topic.
  • A database is a collection of many related tables (and queries, forms, reports).
  • In a relational database, data is kept in tables, and there is a relation between the tables.

DBMS

A database management system (DBMS) is preferred over a flat file system because in a DBMS many users can use the data at the same time, data stays safe, there is no duplication, online access is possible, and data is easily updated. In a flat file system there is only one user, no security, and the problem of duplication. A flat file system is a system without a data dictionary. MS Access is Microsoft's DBMS program — the program for making and managing databases.

Uses of databases in business

In business, databases keep customer records, stock, sales, employees' salaries and accounts. Examples: a shop keeps records of customers and stock; a bank keeps records of accounts.

mcqs.q: Which of the following Microsoft programs is a DBMS?
mcqs.why: MS Access is the program for making and managing databases — Microsoft's DBMS.

mcqs.q: Which statement correctly matches data?
options: Always a unique value in the field
Data in the form of simple facts
mcqs.why: Data are simple facts that have not been arranged.

mcqs.q: Which statement correctly matches the flat file system?
options: Data in the form of simple facts
A system without a data dictionary
mcqs.why: There is no data dictionary in a flat file system — as per the pairing in the book's table.

mcqs.q: Why is a database management system preferred over a flat file system?
options: Many users can use the data at the same time, data stays safe, there is no duplication, and data is easily updated
It keeps all data in a single file
It works for only one user
mcqs.why: In a DBMS, many users can use the data at the same time, data stays safe, there is no duplication, online access is possible, and data is easily updated. In a flat file system, there is only one user, no security, and the problem of duplication.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between a table and a database?
options: A table is one set of arranged rows and columns about one topic; a database is a collection of many related tables
A database is a single row of a table
mcqs.why: A table is one set of arranged rows and columns about one topic; a database is a collection of many related tables (and queries, forms, reports).

mcqs.q: In what form is data kept in a relational database?
mcqs.why: In a relational database, data is kept in tables, and there is a relation between the tables.

mcqs.q: Databases in business are used to keep…
options: customer records, stock, sales, employees' salaries and accounts
mcqs.why: In business, databases keep customer records, stock, sales, employees' salaries and accounts — a shop keeps records of customers and stock; a bank keeps records of accounts.

mcqs.q: A bank uses a database to keep records of…
mcqs.why: A bank keeps records of accounts in its database — one of the book's examples of the use of databases in business.

mcqs.q: Which problem of the flat file system is removed by a DBMS?
mcqs.why: A flat file system has the problem of duplication and only one user; a DBMS removes duplication and lets many users use the data at the same time.

mcqs.q: Besides tables, a database may also contain…
mcqs.why: A database is a collection of many related tables (and queries, forms, reports).

lessons.title: Tables: Records, Fields and Data Types
lessons.notes_html:
Record and field

  • A whole row of one student in the students' table — all the information of one student — is called a record.
  • One piece of information (such as the name) of one student — a column in the table — is called a field. A field is also called an attribute.
  • The basic limit of a flat file system is that it keeps data in a single file.

Data types

  • Students' names come in the String data type, because names are writing (text).
  • Whole numbers are numbers without a decimal point.
  • The data type is fixed in each field so that only the correct kind of data is entered in the field, there are no mistakes, space is saved, and searching/sorting is correct. Example: in a Number field, only numbers can be entered.

Datasheet View and Design View

Datasheet ViewDesign View
Data appears in rows and columns; data can be entered or changedThe structure of the table (field names, data types, properties) appears; the table is designed/changed there

Data redundancy

Data redundancy means the duplication of data — the same data is present again and again.

mcqs.q: What is the basic limit of a flat file system?
options: It does not support MS Access
It keeps data in a single file
mcqs.why: In a flat file system, all the data is in one single file.

mcqs.q: What is a whole row of one student in the students' table called?
mcqs.why: One row in a table (all the information of one student) is called a record.

mcqs.q: What is one piece of information (such as the name) of one student in the students' table called?
mcqs.why: A column of one particular piece of information (such as the name) in a table is called a field.

mcqs.q: Which statement correctly matches a field?
options: Data in the form of simple facts
Attribute — a field is also called an attribute
Always a unique value in the field
mcqs.why: A field is also called an attribute — it holds one particular piece of information, such as the name.

mcqs.q: In which data type do the students' names come in a field?
mcqs.why: Names are writing (text), so their data type is String.

mcqs.q: Data redundancy means … of data.
mcqs.why: Data redundancy means that the same data is present again and again — duplication of data.

mcqs.q: Which statement correctly matches whole-number data?
options: A system without a data dictionary
mcqs.why: Whole numbers are numbers without a decimal point.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between Datasheet View and Design View?
options: Both views show only the structure
Datasheet View is for designing; Design View is for entering data
In Datasheet View data appears in rows and columns and can be entered or changed; in Design View the structure of the table appears and the table is designed there
There is no difference between them
mcqs.why: In Datasheet View, data appears in rows and columns, and data can be entered or changed in it; in Design View, the structure of the table (field names, data types, properties) appears, and the table is designed/changed there.

mcqs.q: Why is the data type fixed in each field?
options: So that the table looks colourful
So that many files are created
So that only the correct kind of data is entered, there are no mistakes, space is saved, and searching/sorting is correct
mcqs.why: The data type is fixed so that only the correct kind of data is entered in the field, there are no mistakes, space is saved, and searching/sorting is correct. Example: in a Number field, only numbers can be entered.

mcqs.q: In a Number field, only which kind of data can be entered?
mcqs.why: The data type fixes the kind of data: in a Number field, only numbers can be entered.

mcqs.q: All the information of one student in one row of the table is a…
mcqs.why: One row in a table (all the information of one student) is called a record; one piece of information, like the name, is a field.

mcqs.q: The name column in the students' table is an example of a…
mcqs.why: A column of one particular piece of information (such as the name) in a table is called a field.

mcqs.q: In Design View of a table, we can see and change…
options: field names, data types and properties
mcqs.why: In Design View, the structure of the table (field names, data types, properties) appears, and the table is designed/changed there.

mcqs.q: Data can be entered or changed in which view?
mcqs.why: In Datasheet View, data appears in rows and columns, and data can be entered or changed in it.

mcqs.q: Fixing the data type of a field helps in…
mcqs.why: Fixing the data type means only the correct kind of data is entered, there are no mistakes, space is saved, and searching/sorting is correct.

lessons.title: Keys and Relations
lessons.notes_html:
Primary key and foreign key

Primary keyForeign key
Uniquely identifies each record in its own tableThe primary key of another table, used in this table so that the two tables can be joined
Never repeated, never empty; its value is always uniqueCreates the link between tables

Relations

A relation is a link between two tables. A one-to-one relation joins one record of one entity with one record of another entity. The book also names one-to-many, many-to-one and many-to-many relations.

Advantages of using relations in a database

  • Duplication of data ends.
  • Data stays consistent and correct.
  • Less space is used.
  • Combined information is easily obtained from many tables.

mcqs.q: What is a field that uniquely identifies each record called?
mcqs.why: A primary key uniquely identifies each record.

mcqs.q: Which relation joins one record of one entity with one record of another entity?
mcqs.why: In a one-to-one relation, one record joins with only one record of another entity.

mcqs.q: Which statement correctly matches the primary key?
options: Always a unique value in the field
Data in the form of simple facts
mcqs.why: The value of a primary key is always unique, because it identifies each record in the table.

mcqs.q: Which statement correctly matches a relation?
options: Always a unique value in the field
A system without a data dictionary
mcqs.why: A relation joins two tables with each other, so that combined information can be obtained from them.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between primary and foreign keys?
options: Both identify records of another table
A foreign key is always unique and never empty in its own table
A primary key uniquely identifies each record in its own table; a foreign key is the primary key of another table used in this table to join the two tables
There is no difference between them
mcqs.why: A primary key uniquely identifies each record in its own table (it is never repeated, never empty); a foreign key is the primary key of another table, used in this table so that the two tables can be joined.

mcqs.q: A primary key is never…
mcqs.why: A primary key uniquely identifies each record in its own table — it is never repeated and never empty.

mcqs.q: Which of the following is an advantage of using relations in a database?
options: Duplication of data ends and data stays consistent and correct
mcqs.why: With relations, duplication of data ends; data stays consistent and correct; less space is used; and combined information is easily obtained from many tables.

mcqs.q: Relations help to obtain … from many tables.
mcqs.why: Combined information is easily obtained from many tables when relations are used.

mcqs.q: A foreign key in a table is actually…
options: the primary key of another table
mcqs.why: A foreign key is the primary key of another table, used in this table so that the two tables can be joined.

mcqs.q: Using relations in a database, space is…
mcqs.why: Duplication of data ends with relations, so less space is used and data stays consistent and correct.

lessons.title: Entities, Attributes and ER Diagrams
lessons.notes_html:
Entity, attribute and relation

TermMeaningExample
EntityAn independent thing — a table with its attributesA student
AttributeA quality of the entityThe student's name, class
RelationThe link between entitiesA student belongs to a class

ERD (Entity-Relationship Diagram)

  • In an ERD, entities, attributes and relations are shown in the form of a diagram.
  • Attributes are shown in an oval shape.
  • With an ERD, the database is correctly designed before making it, mistakes are avoided, time is saved, and the ERD works as documentation/reference.

Reading the book's ER diagram

Entities: Company, Advertisement, Candidate, Interview. Relations: issued, applied for, taken, faced. The company issues the advertisement; the candidate applies for the advertisement; the company takes the interview; the candidate faces the interview. One company can issue many advertisements (one-to-many), and one candidate can face many interviews.

mcqs.q: Which shape is used to show attributes in an ERD?
mcqs.why: In an ERD, attributes are shown in an oval shape.

mcqs.q: Which statement correctly matches an entity?
options: A system without a data dictionary
mcqs.why: An entity is in the form of a table with its attributes.

mcqs.q: In the example 'a student', the student's name and class are its…
mcqs.why: An attribute is a quality of the entity — for the entity 'student', the attributes are the student's name, class, and so on.

mcqs.q: 'A student belongs to a class' is an example of a…
mcqs.why: A relation is the link between entities — for example, a student belongs to a class.

mcqs.q: Why is an ERD important in designing a database?
options: The database is correctly designed before making it, mistakes are avoided, time is saved, and it works as documentation
mcqs.why: In an ERD, entities, attributes and relations are shown in diagram form; with it, the database is correctly designed before making it, mistakes are avoided, time is saved, and the ERD works as documentation/reference.

mcqs.q: In the book's ER diagram, which are the entities?
mcqs.why: The entities in the given ER diagram are Company, Advertisement, Candidate, Interview; its relations are issued, applied for, taken and faced.

mcqs.q: In the book's ER diagram, 'the company issues the advertisement' shows which relation?
mcqs.why: The company issues the advertisement; the candidate applies for the advertisement; the company takes the interview; the candidate faces the interview.

mcqs.q: One company can issue many advertisements — this is which kind of relation?
mcqs.why: One company can issue many advertisements (one-to-many), and one candidate can face many interviews.

mcqs.q: An ERD shows which three things in diagram form?
mcqs.why: In an ERD, entities, attributes and relations are shown in the form of a diagram.

mcqs.q: The ERD also works as … for the database.
mcqs.why: The ERD works as documentation/reference for the database, besides helping in correct design before making it.
